reviews.title: Google’s Corporate Cowardice: It’s Lake Ontario
reviews.text:
★☆☆☆☆

Seeing Lake Ontario labeled “Lake America” in Google Earth is disgusting. A multibillion-dollar corporation helping normalize Trump’s latest nationalist vanity project deserves every bit of criticism it gets. Google’s explanation that it follows official government sources does nothing to make this decision less objectionable.

In my opinion, Trump is the least qualified and most disgraceful people ever to hold the presidency. Google’s willingness to accommodate his political agenda only deepens my disappointment in this company.

Lake Ontario is shared with Canada. Its identity and history deserve more respect than being reduced to a branding exercise for an American president. I use Google Earth to explore the world, and this decision undermines my trust in what it shows me. Corporate cowardice is an ugly look, Google. One star.

reviews.title: Going downhill unfortunately.
reviews.text:
Google Earth used to be a flagship product. It’s now buggy and regularly needs to be restarted.
The first gripe is with the default display mode. I always want satellite imagery, but for some unfathomable reason it wants to open in map mode. What’s the point of using Google Earth in map mode 🤔
The second gripe is that the resolution starts good, but quickly degrades. Only force closing the app and restarting it will solve this problem, and then only for a couple of minutes (if that). 
The third gripe is that adding a dropped pin to a project often (95% of the time) freezes the app, requiring a force close.
There are a host of other gripes, but these 3 need to be solved.

reviews.title: Flakey!  Continually locks up!  Blurry images!  Bizarrely unintuitive UI!
reviews.text:
This app has so many bugs and faults, with a bizarrely unintuitive user interface:

App continually locks-up when saving changes to custom pins - most often when changing pin colour, but can occur at any time.  At other times the app simply crashes.

As many others have mentioned, aerial view goes blurry, most often after returning from Streetview.  

User interface is clunky and bizarrely unintuitive.  It is necessary to divine the weird Google way of doing things - even then many things simply don't work.  

The labels on custom pins don't scale nor disappear when zooming out, leaving the map completely obscured by a hideous mass of white text.  

It isn't possible to select a group of pins and move them to a custom folder.   Each pin has to be copied, pasted into the new folder then the original deleted. 

Cannot select a group of custom pins and set the same property for all.  

Cannot set default properties for custom pins.  

Map randomly zooms out to entire globe for no apparently good reason. 

It is incredibly slow.

Unlike Google Maps, zooming in-and out with two fingers is far too sensitive and is very difficult to avoid reorientating the compass.  Same applies to  moving with one finger.

In summary, it is tedious to do anything in app and infuriatingly frustrating.

For reference; I'm using on a iPad Pro 11 inch (4th Gen) running iPadOS 17.7.2.
